title: Mutable Default Parameter Anti-Pattern
description: Default parameter values are evaluated once when the function is defined. If a mutable object like a list or dictionary is used as a default, mutations persist across every subsequent call to that function.

title: SQL Injection via String Concatenation
description: Constructing SQL queries by concatenating raw user input directly into the query string enables SQL injection attacks. An attacker can manipulate input to execute arbitrary database queries or steal data.

title: Bare Except Clause and Error Swallowing
description: Using a bare 'except:' catches all exceptions, including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, making it impossible to terminate the program properly and hiding critical runtime errors.

title: Unclosed Resource and Missing Context Manager
description: Opening files or network sockets without using a 'with' statement risks resource leaks if exceptions occur before close() is called.
bad_example:
def read_config(path):
    f = open(path, 'r')
    data = f.read()
    f.close()
    return data

title: Hardcoded API Key / Secret Token
description: Hardcoding secrets, API tokens, or passwords into source code exposes credentials to version control and potential unauthorized access.
good_example:
import os
API_KEY = os.getenv('SERVICE_API_KEY')
if not API_KEY:
    raise ValueError('SERVICE_API_KEY environment variable is required')
client = APIClient(api_key=API_KEY)
